# Agents

Roles for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Pi, alone or side by side. Start any role with `ade handover --role <role>`, and run it again after your context is compacted; the records are truer than your own summary. Run anything that may print a lot (tests, builds, logs) as `ade q run -- <command>`: long output is kept whole and you get its head, tail and a handle to page.

## pilot

Flies the board: picks cards, answers needs-judgement stops, decides, lands. Asks a person only through `ade decide --ask`, with a recommendation, a default and a deadline, so silence never stalls the board.

Models and effort: `ade config --roles`. Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash.

## builder

Builds one card in its lane: the smallest change that meets the card's done line.

Models and effort: `ade config --roles`. Tools: Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, Bash.

## reviewer

Reviews one lane diff; answers APPROVE on the first line, or returns a patch.

Models and effort: `ade config --roles`. Tools: Read, Grep, Glob.

## Using ADE

Start with `ade handover --role ROLE`.
Run `ade -h` for the verbs.
Run `ade config WORD` for any setting.
ade.toml is protected: you may run `ade parts set` (and `ade setup`); name any other key to the person, who changes it and reruns `ade init`.
The full guide is the ade skill: `.claude/skills/ade/SKILL.md` or `.agents/skills/ade/SKILL.md`.

- Never answer a question as the person; tell them it waits (`ade decide --desk`).
- A figure in prose or memory is stale, so rerun the command that owns it before quoting it.
